title: Manipulating non-intrinsic outputs of a non-Hermitian coupled system by weak external driving
authors: He Feng, Yi-Fan Xiang, Wei Li, Xue-Hua Wang
abstract: Measurement provides access to exploring and understanding nature and finds widespread applications. It is generally believed that the weak external driving used in measurement introduces negligible disturbance to the intrinsic output of the probed system. Here, we reveal that dissipation in a non-Hermitian quantum coupled system induces interference between self-excitation and coupling-excitation spectral functions, giving rise to non-intrinsic outputs. These non-intrinsic outputs can be effectively manipulated by the ratio of weak external driving strengths applied to two channels, leading to significant phenomena: extreme suppression of dissipation by convergence effect of high-loss mode towards low-loss mode, and giant shift of resonant frequency instead of original spectral Rabi splitting. Crucially, we discover the Pythagorean relation linking eigenlevel splitting, spectral Rabi splitting and average total decay rate, enabling precise measurement of the eigenlevel splitting and coupling strength. Numerical simulations confirm that the interference outputs also exist in classical coupled systems. Our work provides a profound insight into measurement and non-Hermitian physics.
summary: The paper reveals that dissipation in non-Hermitian coupled quantum systems generates 'non-intrinsic' output signals when probed by weak external driving. By controlling the ratio of applied drives, researchers can achieve remarkable effects like suppressing energy loss or inducing giant frequency shifts instead of expected spectral splittings. This offers a new paradigm for manipulating quantum measurements.
main_problem: The work challenges the assumption that weak external driving used in measurement minimally disturbs a probed quantum system, especially when dissipation is present.
main_result: Dissipation induces non-intrinsic outputs through interference between self-excitation and coupling-excitation spectral functions. This allows for on-demand manipulation of these outputs, including extreme loss suppression and giant frequency shifts.
method: The analysis uses theoretical derivations based on solving Heisenberg equations of motion under weak driving, employing the Laplace transform method to calculate spectral responses.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as a non-Hermitian quantum coupled system (e.g., plasmonic modes coupled to emitters) described by an effective Hamiltonian incorporating dissipation ($\Gamma$).
key_observables: Non-intrinsic outputs ($S_{	ext{total}}$), eigenlevel splitting (LS), Spectral Rabi Splitting (SRS), Full Width at Half Maximum (FWHM), and spectral resonance frequency shifts.
important_parameters: Ratio of weak external driving strengths ($E_\# : E_\%$), coupling strength ($g$), and dissipation rates ($\Gamma$).
main_assumptions: The interference effect is shown to originate directly from the presence of dissipation; it vanishes when $\Gamma=0$. The theory is validated across both quantum and classical coupled systems.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate spectral manipulation by varying driving ratios, demonstrating loss suppression (linewidth compression) and the disappearance of SRS under balanced driving conditions. Other figures show frequency shifts in cavity structures.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the non-intrinsic nature of outputs due to dissipation interference, detailing how external driving ratio controls these outputs, deriving a Pythagorean relation linking key spectral parameters, and finally confirming these effects with numerical simulations across various coupling regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides profound insight into measurement backaction in open quantum systems, showing that the measurement process itself can be engineered to yield novel, controllable spectral features beyond intrinsic system properties.
